beliefs.practice: Reuse a single, global MongoClient across the FastAPI app (create it at startup and close at shutdown); set a sensible maxPoolSize (e.g., 50) and serverSelectionTimeoutMS (e.g., 5000) to avoid creating/tearing down clients per request.
Never store the DOCUMENTDB_URI or other credentials in source control; load the connection string from an environment variable and keep a .env.example with a placeholder instead.
Put the production connection secret into a secrets store (Azure Key Vault) and have the app read it at startup rather than hard-coding or committing it; do not log full connection strings anywhere.

Enforce row-level access by always including patientId in the DB query filter (e.g., find({ patientId: X, ... })) rather than relying solely on app-layer checks; add an index on patientId for these queries.

Model each chunk document with explicit fields: patientId, chunkId (unique), sourceId, position, text, embedding (vector), createdAt; create a unique index on chunkId and an index on patientId + createdAt for efficient retrieval and audit.
Keep chunk document sizes well under MongoDB's 16MB document limit (target <= 50–200 KB per chunk); choose chunk token sizes (e.g., 200–500 tokens) to balance context and storage/latency.

Create and maintain a vector index on the embedding field with the correct dimensionality and distance metric (e.g., dimensions: 1536, metric: 'cosine') so DB-side ANN search is available instead of full-collection scans.

If using DB-side vector indexes, explicitly choose and configure the ANN algorithm (e.g., HNSW with parameters efConstruction/M and efSearch or DiskANN/IVF params) tuned for recall/latency tradeoffs and document counts.

If the cluster lacks or you can't trust DB-side vector search, use the DB to prefilter by patientId and any metadata and then re-rank a limited candidate set in-application using cosine similarity; limit candidates (e.g., top 200) to bound CPU.

Create a compound index for common query patterns (e.g., { patientId: 1, sourceId: 1, position: 1 }) to support retrieving context windows quickly and avoid collection scans when assembling summaries.
Project only required fields in queries (e.g., { text:1, chunkId:1 }) to reduce network egress and latency when returning candidate chunks for summarization.
Avoid using skip-based pagination for large offsets; use range- or cursor-based pagination (e.g., _id or createdAt) for predictable performance when enumerating a patient's records.

Implement robust retry logic with exponential backoff for transient errors; specifically handle HTTP 429 / TooManyRequests from Cosmos DB by honoring Retry-After and backing off, and make writes idempotent when retrying.

Set retryWrites=true / retryWrites option for the driver when appropriate, and ensure idempotency for multi-step operations (e.g., use upsert with unique chunkId to avoid duplicate chunks on retries).

Provision adequate throughput (RU/s or cluster tier) for expected vector search and embedding write load; monitor RU consumption and increase throughput or enable autoscale to avoid 429 throttling during bulk ingestion (seed.py).

Use TLS encryption for connections (ensure the connection string uses tls=true or equivalent) and restrict network access via firewall rules, VNet, or private endpoint so the DB is not publicly exposed.
Enable collection-level auditing / diagnostic logs (slow query and request telemetry) in Azure Monitor so you can trace slow summary queries and vector searches and correlate to RU consumption.

When storing embeddings, store them in a consistent numeric type and shape (e.g., float32 arrays) and persist the embedding dimension as metadata to validate inputs before inserting or querying the vector index.

Index any frequently-filtered metadata fields (e.g., patientId, sourceId, tags) and avoid wide unindexed scans for RAG retrieval; periodically review index usage and drop unused indexes to reduce write overhead.

Keep a deterministic canonicalization for text chunks (strip PHI consistently per policy, normalize whitespace, store original offsets) so reassembly and references in answers reliably map back to source locations.

Unit and integration tests should mock the DB for fast CI and include at least one integration test against a real/dev cluster to validate indexes and vector-search behavior; do not run integration tests that modify production DB.
Avoid transferring full embeddings from DB on every request—either perform ANN in DB or store a compact index/hashes and only fetch embeddings for a small candidate set to re-rank in-app.

When seeding large numbers of chunks, use bulk/ordered bulk writes and monitor RU usage; throttle ingestion and use exponential backoff on 429 rather than retrying aggressively from many concurrent workers.

Protect PHI in transit and at rest: ensure DB-level encryption is enabled (managed by Azure), restrict export of full documents in logs or error traces, and consider client-side field-level encryption for highly sensitive fields.

For query correctness and latency, test and assert that any application-side re-ranking (cosine similarity) uses the same distance metric and normalization as the DB-side vector index to avoid retrieval/recall mismatches.
